This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/scenarios`, touching **29** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/qa/scenarios/README.md`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/qa/scenarios/README.md`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **5** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **63** of **226** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **163** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **163**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **104** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **0** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json aa3e21cca7ec885a8325eb24e9c31e11ed5e3453` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `184c711c68f77c647ded91cd6c218a7f8b330022` — the merge of head `fdac4b9b5a505f1b293de3e2b20919ad88b296f5` into base `aa3e21cca7ec885a8325eb24e9c31e11ed5e3453`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 184c711c68f77c647ded91cd6c218a7f8b330022 && git checkout 184c711c68f77c647ded91cd6c218a7f8b330022
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin aa3e21cca7ec885a8325eb24e9c31e11ed5e3453 fdac4b9b5a505f1b293de3e2b20919ad88b296f5 && git checkout -B drift-repro aa3e21cca7ec885a8325eb24e9c31e11ed5e3453 && git merge --no-ff fdac4b9b5a505f1b293de3e2b20919ad88b296f5

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json aa3e21cca7ec885a8325eb24e9c31e11ed5e3453
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs aa3e21cca7ec885a8325eb24e9c31e11ed5e3453` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对 — ACCEPT · domain:devx#3 · `Head-sha: fdac4b9b5a505f1b293de3e2b20919ad88b296f5` · 2026-11-07T11:01Z

Reviewed against GitHub at the head above, not against the report's own account.

- **Shape:** draft, base `main`, line 1 `Fixes #31106`. A closing-keyword scan of the whole body finds no other card number.
- **Premise, measured:** at origin/main `a61f61a4`, `driver.ts:285` read `maxTurnsAuthor ?? 80`, `:311` read `maxTurnsAsk ?? 12`, and neither flag existed under `src/runner/`.
- **File surface:** `GET /pulls/31111/files` lists 8 paths, all inside the claim (6705412456): `src/runner/{driver,cli,orchestrate,scorecard,transcript}.ts`, `test/runner/{units,orchestrate}.test.ts`, and the README. `src/schema.ts` is read only. `check-governed-merges --pr 31111`: NOT governed, 288 changed lines, ≤ 3000.
- **Changeset:** `skip-changeset` is accepted (`@objectstack/scenarios` is `private: true`).
- **Rulings held:**
  - The cost ruling: `API_BILLING_ENV` / `ApiBillingRefusedError` are untouched.
  - Ruling D: there is no scoring change.
  - `error_max_turns` still makes "author turn failed" (#31096). Only the cap moves.
- **Spot reads:**
  - `DEFAULT_AUTHOR_MAX_TURNS = { control: 80, starter: 300, delivery: 600 }` and `DEFAULT_ASK_MAX_TURNS = 12`.
  - `--author-max-turns` overrides every tier alike. Both flags refuse anything that is not a whole number above 0.
  - `makeDriver` refuses all three limit flags on a replay.
  - `AuthorTask.tier` is required, and all three `driver.author` calls in `orchestrate.ts` (scratch build, scratch iterate, template iterate) pass `card.tier`. The replay key is unchanged, so recordings still replay.
  - The cap used rides `meta.process.maxTurns`, `TurnSummary.maxTurns`, the scorecard author row (`N/cap turns`) and `DriverInfo`.
- **Accepted deviations:**
  - (1) The card's example defaults are kept, with the measured reason in the PR body. At 11–18 s per turn, the 300 cap and the 60-minute `--author-timeout` bind at about the same point for a `starter` build.
  - (2) The ask cap stays 12 on every tier, because no ask turn has a measured `error_max_turns`.
  - (3) `origin/main` was not merged before the PR. 4 commits landed since the base, none touching this package; CI tests the merge ref.
  - (4) `test:repo` was not run locally. The one repo-level pin that reads this package enumerates `referenceTargetOf` callers, and this diff adds none (`git diff … | grep -c referenceTargetOf` = 0).
- **Gates (check-runs at this head, read 2026-11-07T11:01Z):** 48 total, 23 success, 18 skipped, 7 still running, 0 failure. Landing waits for every check to be green or an expected skip. Local: 49 of 49 derived families exited 0 (one re-run after its prerequisite was built); package tests 431/431; six ablations each turned red and were restored.
- **Out of scope:** a `delivery` card would hit the 60-minute clock before its 600-turn cap. 0 of 9 cards are `delivery` today. This is documented in the constant and the README; noted, not filed.
- **Landing:** when every check is green, the seat sends `pr_ready` + `automerge_enable` through the relay. `mcp_calls` 0.
